name: paralegal
description: Legal assistant / paralegal fundamentals: legal terminology, court procedures, contract law, legal research, document preparation, and ethics. Built on top of high-school-graduate base.

facts.fact: Civil law deals with disputes between individuals or organizations, while criminal law deals with offenses against the state or society
facts.query: civil law criminal law disputes offenses

facts.fact: A plaintiff is the party who brings a lawsuit, and the defendant is the party being sued
The burden of proof in a civil case is preponderance of the evidence, meaning more likely than not
facts.query: burden of proof civil preponderance evidence

facts.fact: The burden of proof in a criminal case is beyond a reasonable doubt, which is a higher standard than civil cases
facts.query: burden of proof criminal beyond reasonable doubt

facts.fact: The US court system includes federal courts (district, circuit appellate, Supreme Court) and state courts (trial, appellate, supreme)
facts.query: court system federal state appellate supreme

facts.fact: Jurisdiction is the authority of a court to hear and decide a case, based on subject matter and geographic location
A statute is a law passed by a legislature, while common law is based on judicial precedent from prior court decisions
Stare decisis is the principle that courts follow prior decisions (precedent) to ensure consistency in the law
A tort is a civil wrong that causes harm, for which the injured party can seek compensation, such as negligence or defamation
facts.query: tort civil wrong negligence defamation compensation

facts.fact: A felony is a serious crime punishable by more than one year in prison, while a misdemeanor is a less serious offense
A contract is a legally binding agreement between two or more parties that creates enforceable obligations
The four elements of a valid contract are: offer, acceptance, consideration, and mutual assent (meeting of the minds)
Consideration is something of value exchanged by the parties, such as money, goods, or services, and is required for a contract to be enforceable
A breach of contract occurs when one party fails to fulfill their obligations under the agreement
Damages are the monetary compensation awarded to the injured party for a breach of contract
An offer can be revoked by the offeror any time before it is accepted, unless it is supported by consideration or an option contract
A void contract has no legal effect from the beginning, while a voidable contract is valid but can be canceled by one party
facts.query: void voidable contract legal effect cancel

facts.fact: The statute of frauds requires certain contracts (like real estate sales over one year) to be in writing to be enforceable
facts.query: statute of frauds writing real estate

facts.fact: An indemnity clause shifts risk from one party to another, requiring one party to compensate the other for certain losses
A force majeure clause excuses performance when unforeseeable events beyond a party's control prevent fulfillment of the contract
facts.query: force majeure clause unforeseeable events excuse

facts.fact: Case law is the body of legal decisions from prior court cases that serve as precedent for future cases
A legal citation identifies a case or statute, typically including the case name, volume, reporter, page number, and year
facts.query: legal citation case volume reporter page

facts.fact: Westlaw and LexisNexis are major commercial legal research databases for searching cases, statutes, and secondary sources
A brief is a written summary of a court case, including the facts, issues, holding, and reasoning
facts.query: brief case summary facts issues holding

facts.fact: IRAC stands for Issue, Rule, Analysis, Conclusion, which is a method for organizing legal analysis
Secondary sources like legal encyclopedias, treatises, and law review articles explain and interpret primary law but are not binding
facts.query: secondary sources encyclopedia treatise law review

facts.fact: Shepardizing (or Shepardizing) is the process of checking whether a case has been overruled, affirmed, or criticized by later decisions
A statute is organized into titles, chapters, and sections, and must be read in the context of the entire code
A complaint is the initial pleading filed by a plaintiff that starts a lawsuit, stating the claims and requesting relief
An answer is the defendant's response to the complaint, admitting or denying each allegation and raising defenses
A motion is a formal request to the court asking for a specific ruling or order
Discovery is the pre-trial process where parties exchange information, including interrogatories, depositions, and document requests
An affidavit is a written statement made under oath, signed in front of a notary public
A power of attorney is a legal document authorizing one person to act on behalf of another in legal or financial matters
facts.query: power of attorney authorize act behalf

facts.fact: A will (last will and testament) directs how a person's property is distributed after death and names an executor
A retainer agreement is a contract between a lawyer and client that establishes the scope of representation and fee arrangement
facts.query: retainer agreement lawyer client fee scope

facts.fact: A bill of sale is a document that transfers ownership of personal property from a seller to a buyer
facts.query: bill of sale transfer ownership personal property

facts.fact: A notary public is an official authorized to witness signatures, administer oaths, and verify document authenticity
facts.query: notary public witness signatures oaths verify

facts.fact: Attorney-client privilege protects confidential communications between a lawyer and client from being disclosed in court
The duty of confidentiality requires lawyers and paralegals to keep client information private, even after the representation ends
facts.query: duty of confidentiality client information private

facts.fact: A conflict of interest occurs when a lawyer's duty to one client conflicts with duties to another client or their own interests
facts.query: conflict of interest lawyer client duty

facts.fact: The duty of loyalty requires legal professionals to put the client's interests first, within the bounds of the law
facts.query: duty of loyalty client interests first

facts.fact: Unauthorized practice of law (UPL) occurs when a non-lawyer provides legal advice or services, which is prohibited
facts.query: unauthorized practice of law non-lawyer advice prohibited

facts.fact: A paralegal must work under the supervision of a licensed attorney and cannot give legal advice independently
facts.query: paralegal supervision attorney no legal advice

facts.fact: Model Rules of Professional Conduct are ethical guidelines for lawyers, adopted with variations by state bar associations
facts.query: model rules professional conduct ethics bar

facts.fact: The duty of competence requires legal professionals to have the necessary skill and knowledge to handle a client's matter
facts.query: duty of competence skill knowledge client
